web-pages.admin.code.linkHint: Signing in through this link fills in the invite code when creating a workspace.

web-pages.admin.code.madeLead.other: Send them the code or link. Single use, expires in {n} days.

web-pages.admin.code.revokeBody: The code can no longer create a workspace, and sign-up links already sent stop working.
web-pages.admin.fb.copied: Copied, ready to paste to an agent
web-pages.admin.noPermission.title: No access
web-pages.admin.pending.addLead: They don't need to sign in first: these apply when they first sign in with this email. Accounts that have already signed in with it get them immediately.
web-pages.admin.pending.added: Added. Takes effect on first sign-in
web-pages.admin.pending.known: This email has signed in before; granted immediately
web-pages.admin.search.feedback: Search title, content, reporter, station, workspace, FB #
web-pages.admin.title: Admin
web-pages.admin.user.blockBody: Signs them out on all devices and blocks future sign-in. Their workspaces and contents stay as they are. You can unblock them anytime.
web-pages.admin.ws.deleteBody: All members are removed; its stations disconnect and must join another workspace. Can't be undone.
web-pages.about.perf.note: Every 5 s, writes CPU use, busiest threads, thermal state and frame rate to {where} on this device ({size} so far). Never uploaded.
web-pages.about.perf.noteFolder: Every 5 s, writes CPU use, memory and frame rate to {where} on this device ({size} so far). Never uploaded. Errors are kept in that folder too, whether this is on or not.

web-pages.appearance.theme.title: Theme
web-pages.appearance.accent.title: Accent color

web-pages.appearance.title: Appearance
web-pages.appearance.motion.title: Motion
web-pages.appearance.haptics.title: Haptics

web-pages.appearance.chatPage.title: Try the new chat page
web-pages.appearance.chatPage.descriptio: A new message list: what you read stays put. Still being completed; turn it off if something is wrong
web-pages.appearance.drop.title: Files dragged into a chat
web-pages.appearance.drop.description: Path tells the agent where the file is; File puts it on the chat's station
web-pages.appearance.archive.title: Archive suggestions
web-pages.appearance.archive.description: Whether a finished chat suggests archiving it: faded in the sidebar. Only on this device; the archive button in the bar, its shortcut and the context menu stay either way.
web-pages.appearance.archive.offHint: Finished chats look as usual; archive them yourself when you like.
web-pages.appearance.archive.doneHint: Suggested once every agent said it is done, nothing waits for your decision and you have read it. It goes by these states, not by what was said; where the station has archive suggestions on, by the model's review.
web-pages.appearance.archive.reviewedHin: Suggested only for chats the station's archive suggestions (Settings → Automatic decisions) found to have nothing left. Stations without archive suggestions on suggest none.
web-pages.appearance.fonts.title: Fonts
web-pages.appearance.fonts.description: The fonts for the interface, messages and code
web-pages.appearance.fonts.sampleRow: The quick brown fox 天地玄黄 0O 1lI
web-pages.appearance.fonts.sampleMine: The sign-in button does nothing in Safari
web-pages.appearance.fonts.sampleText: The click was swallowed by `preventDefault` before the form was sent; it is handled in `onSubmit` now:
web-pages.archive.about: Chats archived manually, plus finished chats idle for over a day (not running, not blocked, no unread messages). A chat returns to the list when it gets a new message.
web-pages.archive.deleteText: Its session, chat history and workspace folder will be deleted. This can't be undone.
web-pages.archive.title: Archived
web-pages.archiving.title: Archive
web-pages.archiving.auto.title: Automatic archiving
web-pages.archiving.auto.description: A station puts finished chats that have been idle for a while into the archive on its own: nothing running, nothing waiting for someone, nothing unread by whoever started it. Archived chats can be restored any time; pinned and kept chats are never archived on their own. Each station has its own setting, which only workspace managers can change.
web-pages.archiving.mode.offHint: This station archives no chat on its own; archive them by hand.
web-pages.archiving.mode.idleHint: Archived once idle for the days below. It goes by states, not by what was said: something mentioned but left undone goes unnoticed.
web-pages.archiving.mode.reviewedHint: Archived once idle for the days below and the archive suggestions found nothing left to do.
web-pages.archiving.reviewNeeded: This station has archive suggestions off, so no chat is archived on its own for now.
web-pages.archiving.hintNoReview: No station has archive suggestions on, so After review suggests nothing; turn them on in Automatic decisions to use it.
web-pages.archiving.hintSomeReview: Only {on} has archive suggestions on; chats on {off} are not suggested.
web-pages.archiving.stationNeedsReview: To choose After review, turn on this station's archive suggestions first.
web-pages.archiving.stalled: After review, but archive suggestions are off: nothing is archived for now
web-pages.archiving.adminOnly: Only workspace managers can change this.
web-pages.archiving.slackHint: Archived even when waiting for a reply, as nobody answers them in still.fail; they come back when someone speaks in Slack.
web-pages.archiving.upgrade: Update this station to set automatic archiving
web-pages.archivePolicy.chats: Chats classified as this in the last {days} days
web-pages.archivePolicy.name: Name
web-pages.archivePolicy.rubric: When a chat fits this option
web-pages.archivePolicy.saved: Archive policy saved; finished chats will be rechecked under the new policy
web-pages.archivePolicy.textLead: The decision model reads this first when judging a chat; options are listed below
web-pages.archivePolicy.title: Archive policy

web-pages.automaticDecisions.choosePoint: Choose a decision point, then configure each station’s model

web-pages.chat.pickSaved: Changed. Applies from the next turn
web-pages.cloud.slackInstalled.doneBody: Back in {name}, add the app's App-Level Token on the Connects page to finish. You can close this page.
web-pages.cloud.slackInstalled.handing: Handing the install off to the station
web-pages.cloud.slackInstalled.notInstal: Slack didn't allow the install. Go back to {name} and click “Install to workspace” again.
web-pages.cloud.slackInstalled.signInBod: Sign in with the account that created this app to hand the install to the station. Then click “Install to workspace” in {name} again.
web-pages.connect.bothRuntimes: This model runs on both runtimes.
web-pages.connect.chooseLead: From now on, messages to “{name}” go to the chosen session. The previous session is kept but no longer receives new messages from this connect.
web-pages.connect.deleteBody: Disconnects from Slack. You need to delete the app in Slack yourself.

web-pages.connect.deleteBodySessions.one: Disconnects from Slack. Its 1 session keeps its history but gets no new messages. You need to delete the app in Slack yourself.
web-pages.connect.deleteBodySessions.other: Disconnects from Slack. Its {n} sessions keep their history but get no new messages. You need to delete the app in Slack yourself.

web-pages.connect.effects.mentionOnly: From now on, only @-mentioned threads go into a session. Replies in threads already in a session still arrive.
web-pages.connect.effects.newSingle: The next message starts a new single session. You can also pick an existing one after switching.
web-pages.connect.effects.noMention: No @ needed: every message in channels and DMs it can see goes to the agent. Usage goes up noticeably.
web-pages.connect.effects.resumeSingle: Resumes the single session it was bound to.

web-pages.connect.effects.running.one: 1 session is running and will finish its current turn.
web-pages.connect.effects.running.other: {n} sessions are running and will finish their current turn.

web-pages.connect.effects.switchBack: Switching back to single session resumes the same one.
web-pages.connect.effects.threadsRestart: To continue a thread from the single session, @ it again. That starts a new session without the old context.
web-pages.connect.effects.toMulti: The bound session stops getting messages. Each thread gets its own session when @-mentioned.
web-pages.connect.effects.toSingle: All messages go into one session. Existing per-thread sessions stop getting messages, including replies in their threads. History is kept.
web-pages.connect.effects.toSingle.feish: From now on every message it gets goes to one session; the groups' current sessions get no new messages. Their history is kept.
web-pages.connect.effects.toMulti.feishu: The bound session gets no new messages. From now on each group starts its own session when it is mentioned.
web-pages.connect.effects.threadsRestart: To go on in a group, mention it again: that starts a new session without the earlier context.
web-pages.connect.effects.mentionOnly.fe: From now on only groups where it is mentioned go to the session; messages in groups already in it still arrive.
web-pages.connect.effects.noMention.feis: No @ needed: every message in every group and chat it is in goes to the agent, which uses noticeably more.
web-pages.connect.effects.toThreads.feis: From now on, each thread starts its own session when it is @-mentioned, and replies stay in the thread. Existing group sessions stop receiving new messages. Their history is kept.
web-pages.connect.effects.toGroups.feish: From now on, each group starts one session when it is @-mentioned, and replies go to the group. Existing thread sessions stop receiving new messages. Their history is kept.
web-pages.connect.effects.singleToThread: The bound session stops receiving new messages. From now on, each thread starts its own session when it is @-mentioned, and replies stay in the thread.
web-pages.connect.everyMessageSentence: Every message it sees goes into the session.
web-pages.connect.made.appToken: On the Socket Mode page, generate an App-Level Token and copy it (starts with xapp-; scopes are preset).
web-pages.connect.made.manual: App created. Install it to the workspace, then copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…) from the OAuth page.
web-pages.connect.made.oauth: App created. Install it to the workspace and click “Allow” in Slack; the bot token goes to the station automatically.
web-pages.connect.manualApp: Create the app in Slack and paste tokens
web-pages.connect.mentionOff: Every message it sees in channels goes into the session.
web-pages.connect.mentionOn: Replies in an @-mentioned thread need no further @.
web-pages.connect.modeLead: This changes which session each subsequent message goes into. Ongoing chats may be cut off; review the effects below before confirming.
web-pages.connect.noModels: No models listed by the profile · View profiles
web-pages.connect.noModelsFor: No models listed by the {runtime} profile · View profiles
web-pages.connect.noSession: No session yet. The next message starts one.
web-pages.connect.startsOnLead: Pick the station new conversations with this bot run on. Conversations already going keep running where they are.
web-pages.connect.moveLead: The connect, with its tokens, runs on the station you pick from then on. Its chats keep running where they are, and their messages go through it there.
web-pages.connect.moveNone: No other station of this workspace is online.
web-pages.connect.ownerLead: The owner decides whose “Created by me” list it appears in. Workspace owners, admins and the current owner can change it.
web-pages.connect.recentNone: No sessions yet. @{name} in Slack to start one.
web-pages.connect.replaceLead: You can replace just one. Leave the other empty to keep the saved value.
web-pages.connect.runtimeChanges: Runs on {runtime}. New chats use the new settings; a single session switches from its next message.
web-pages.connect.runtimeNote: Runs on {runtime}, fixed after creation; for another runtime, create a new connect. A single session switches models from its next message.
web-pages.connect.runtimeChanges.multi: Runs on {runtime}. New chats use the new settings.
web-pages.connect.runtimeNote.multi: Runs on {runtime}, fixed after creation; for another runtime, create a new connect.
web-pages.connect.teamLead: Choose the Slack workspace whose configuration token will create the app.
web-pages.connect.tokenWhy: With it, {name} creates the Slack app for you: set its name, avatar and permissions here instead of in Slack's admin. Only you can use it; others on this station can't see it.
web-pages.connect.feishu.name: Feishu
web-pages.connect.feishu.slackNote: Use it in Slack channels and DMs
web-pages.connect.comma.note: Its agents work in the Tasks Comma gives them
web-pages.connect.comma.lineHint: In Comma, add the still.fail plugin: it shows a line starting with comma. Paste it here.
web-pages.connect.feishu.feishuNote: Use it in Feishu groups and chats, Lark included
web-pages.connect.feishu.scanNote: Scan with Feishu to create and set up the bot
web-pages.connect.feishu.appNote: Enter the App ID and App Secret from the developer console
web-pages.connect.feishu.qr: QR code to create the Feishu bot
web-pages.connect.feishu.scanHint: With Feishu on this device, you can also open it here
web-pages.connect.feishu.appHint: The app needs the bot capability and long connection on, the message event and card callback subscribed, the permissions granted and a version published.
web-pages.connect.feishu.larkNote: Turn on for an app made on larksuite.com
web-pages.connect.feishu.replaceLead: The new App Secret is verified before it is saved. The connect then reconnects.
web-pages.connect.mentionOn.feishu: Once mentioned, later messages in the same group need no @.
web-pages.connect.mentionOff.feishu: Every message in the groups it is in goes to the session.
web-pages.connect.recentNone.feishu: No sessions yet. @-mention {name} in a group or message it directly to start
web-pages.connect.deleteBody.feishu: It disconnects. You need to delete the app in the developer console yourself.

web-pages.connect.deleteBodySessions.fei.one: It disconnects. Its 1 session keeps its history but gets no new messages. You need to delete the app in the developer console yourself.
web-pages.connect.deleteBodySessions.fei.other: It disconnects. Its {n} sessions keep their history but get no new messages. You need to delete the app in the developer console yourself.

web-pages.connect.recentNone.comma: No sessions yet. Each Task Comma gives it starts a session of its own.
web-pages.connect.deleteBody.comma: Disconnects from Comma. To remove this device from Comma as well, do so on Comma's still.fail plugin page or the still.fail page of Comma for Teams.

web-pages.connect.deleteBodySessions.com.one: Disconnects from Comma. Its 1 session keeps its history but gets no new messages. To remove this device from Comma as well, do so on Comma's still.fail plugin page or the still.fail page of Comma for Teams.
web-pages.connect.deleteBodySessions.com.other: Disconnects from Comma. Its {n} sessions keep their history but get no new messages. To remove this device from Comma as well, do so on Comma's still.fail plugin page or the still.fail page of Comma for Teams.

web-pages.connects.about: A connect is how people reach {name}, such as a Slack app. Each lives on a station and is bound to a model.
web-pages.connects.addFirstLead: A connect lets people @ an agent in Slack: a Slack app linked to a station.
web-pages.connects.noOnline: No stations online. Add a connect once a station is back online.
web-pages.connects.profileFirstLead: Connects run models through a profile. Add one first.
web-pages.connects.removeBody: Removes it from {name} only. The app stays in Slack; delete it in Slack's app settings if unused.
web-pages.errors.inviteCodeInvalid: Invalid invite code. Check for typos.
web-pages.errors.inviteCodeRequired: The free plan includes 1 workspace; creating another requires an invite code
web-pages.errors.tooManyMembers: Member limit reached: only you on the free plan, up to 6 people on Standard
web-pages.errors.tooManyWorkspaces: An account can create up to 5 workspaces
web-pages.notifications.kinds.doneNote: An agent finished a turn you haven't read
web-pages.notifications.kinds.failedNote: A turn failed or an agent couldn't start
web-pages.notifications.kinds.messageNot: Someone else posts in a chat you're in
web-pages.notifications.kinds.servicesNo: A web service or background job has been up over an hour
web-pages.notifications.kinds.title: Notification types
web-pages.notifications.kinds.waitNote: An agent is waiting on you: a card, or it needs your help
web-pages.notifications.noteDevice: This device only; no alerts for the chat you're viewing
web-pages.notifications.sound: Sound is controlled by the system: System Settings → Notifications → {name} → Play sound for notifications.
web-pages.profiles.addModelPlaceholder: Add a model by name, e.g. qwen3.8-flash
web-pages.profiles.background: Background running commands on new messages
web-pages.profiles.backgroundOff: New messages wait until the running command or subagent finishes
web-pages.profiles.backgroundOn: While Claude Code waits on a command or subagent, a new message moves it to the background (like Ctrl+B). The agent reads the message immediately and handles the results when they finish.
web-pages.profiles.deleteBody: Removes it from {name} only. The config folder and its sign-in are kept. Sessions using it switch to another Profile, or stop if none is available.
web-pages.profiles.deviceCodeNote: On the OpenAI page, sign in with the ChatGPT account for {name} and paste the code. This page continues automatically. If device code sign-in is off, turn it on in ChatGPT's security settings first.
web-pages.profiles.deviceCodeNoteOpencod: On the OpenCode page that opens, sign in, check that its code matches this one, then choose the workspace with Go and authorize. This page continues by itself once you are done.
web-pages.profiles.deviceCodeNoteKimi: On the Kimi page that opens, sign in with the account that has Kimi Code, check that the code matches, then authorize. This page continues by itself once you are done.
web-pages.profiles.deviceCodeNoteGrok: On the xAI page that opens, sign in with the account that has SuperGrok or X Premium+, enter the code, then approve. This page continues by itself once you are done.
web-pages.profiles.deviceCodeNoteCursor: On the Cursor page that opens, sign in and confirm. This page continues by itself once you are done.
web-pages.profiles.disableBody: {name} stops using {runtime}'s sign-in on this machine. The sign-in itself is kept and can be used again later. Sessions using it switch to another Profile, or stop if none is available.
web-pages.profiles.disableCopyBody: This station stops using this shared Profile; the station sharing it is not affected, and it can be enabled here again. Sessions using it move to another Profile, or stop if none is available.
web-pages.profiles.disableKeyBody: The key and its settings are kept, and can be enabled again. Sessions using it move to another Profile, or stop if none is available. Stations with shared copies sync the disabled state after they update.
web-pages.stations.agentEnvLead: Agents, logins and tasks started by this station load these variables, commonly to set an HTTP proxy. One NAME=value per line; you can paste a .env file. Leave a masked value as it is to keep it. A Profile's variable of the same name takes precedence. After saving, idle agent processes restart; running ones pick up the change after their current turn.
web-pages.profiles.envLead: The runtime starts with these variables to reach your model service. {route} in a value is replaced with the session's route ID.
web-pages.profiles.envSaved: Saved {masked}. Leave empty to keep it
web-pages.profiles.fastLead: Applies to sessions that follow the account. Fast uses more quota or credits.
web-pages.profiles.keychainTip: This sign-in is in a keychain the station can't read. Sign in separately for {name}; this machine's existing sign-in is unaffected.
web-pages.profiles.lead: What agents use to run models: {subscription} or a model service key
web-pages.profiles.machineAdded: Profile added with this machine's sign-in
web-pages.profiles.machineLoginAbout: To switch accounts, sign in again, or sign out, use {runtime} on this machine; this profile follows those changes. To stop using it, disable it from the top-right menu.
web-pages.profiles.manual: Or sign in manually on the server
web-pages.profiles.modelsAbout: Every listed model can be chosen for new chats and connects
web-pages.profiles.modelsAboutNone: After the profile is checked, its available models appear here.
web-pages.profiles.name: Name
web-pages.profiles.signInNote: Sign-in happens on the machine hosting {name}; you only need to authorize in the browser
web-pages.profiles.signedInSwitch: Signed in. Sign in again to switch accounts.
web-pages.profiles.signingInNote: Finish within 15 minutes, or it's canceled automatically
web-pages.profiles.step1: Open the auth page, sign in with the Claude account for {name}, and approve
web-pages.profiles.step1Devin: Open the auth page and sign in with the Devin account for {name}
web-pages.profiles.step2Devin: After signing in, the page shows a code. Paste it here:
web-pages.profiles.step2: After approving, the page shows a code. Paste it here:
web-pages.profiles.useMachineTip: Uses this machine's sign-in as is, and follows it if you switch accounts or sign out there
web-pages.profiles.usageNone: Not used in the last 7 days
web-pages.settings.account.sessionsLead: Browsers and devices where this account is signed in to {name}. Sign out any you don't recognize.
web-pages.settings.account.signOutConfir: This device stops using the account, and its workspaces are removed from here. Other accounts aren't affected.
web-pages.settings.account.signOutHereBo: Its workspaces are removed from here. Other accounts aren't affected.
web-pages.settings.account.deleteConfirm: The account {email} will be deleted. Workspaces only you are in are deleted with it, and their stations leave them; the other workspaces you're in remove you. Chats and files on stations are on your own machines and aren't affected. This can't be undone.
web-pages.settings.account.deleteHereBod: Deleted from {name} for good. Chats and files on stations aren't affected.
web-pages.settings.enroll.run: Run in a terminal on that machine

web-pages.settings.members.addedNote.one: 1 person · Joins on first sign-in to {name}
web-pages.settings.members.addedNote.other: {n} people · Join on first sign-in to {name}

web-pages.settings.memory.lead: Memory shared by all chats on a station: global memory spans projects, and each project has its own. Each station keeps its own memory; nothing syncs between stations.
web-pages.settings.memory.title: Memory
web-pages.settings.prices.lead: Unit prices each station uses to estimate cost
web-pages.settings.prices.title: Prices
web-pages.settings.profiles.lead: A profile is the account agents use to run models: a subscription, or a key for a model service. Each profile runs on its station, and {name} sets up which runtimes it can use.
web-pages.settings.profiles.offlineAdd: Offline. Add it once it's online
web-pages.settings.relays.hint: An iroh-relay https address. The web app requires a publicly issued certificate (such as Let's Encrypt); self-signed certificates aren't supported.
web-pages.settings.relays.lead: This workspace's stations and members' devices also connect through these relays in addition to {name}'s, using the fastest one. Unreachable relays are skipped.
web-pages.settings.relays.title: Relays
web-pages.settings.stations.existingLead: Add a station you manage in another workspace here too
web-pages.settings.stations.existingNone: No stations in the other workspaces you manage can be added
web-pages.settings.stations.noneYet: No stations yet. An admin needs to add one.
web-pages.settings.stations.removeConfir: It disconnects from {name} cloud, and members lose access from here. {name} and data on that machine stay, and you can add it back later.
web-pages.settings.stations.softIsolatio: Agents on that machine run as the same system user: each workspace's chats, memory, Slack and folders are kept apart, but it isn't a sandbox
web-pages.localStation.title: This machine's station
web-pages.localStation.lead: Manage the station on this Mac here, whether it comes with the {name} app or is installed separately. Which workspace it joins is set in each workspace's Station settings.
web-pages.localStation.leadPc: Manage the station on this PC here, whether it comes with the {name} app or is installed separately. Which workspace it joins is set in each workspace's Station settings.
web-pages.localStation.openFolderFiles: Show data in the file manager
web-pages.settings.title: Settings
web-pages.settings.usage.lead: Tokens used by agents on each station, priced at API rates, by person, chat, account and model. Visible to everyone in the workspace.
web-pages.settings.usage.title: Usage
web-pages.settings.workspace.deleteBody: Members lose access and stations disconnect from {name} cloud. Station data stays.

web-pages.settings.workspace.deleteConfi.one: All members lose access, and 1 station disconnects from {name} cloud (its data stays)
web-pages.settings.workspace.deleteConfi.other: All members lose access, and {n} stations disconnect from {name} cloud (their data stays)

web-pages.settings.workspace.leaveConfir: You'll lose access to its stations until you're invited back

web-pages.slackApp.group.base.descriptio: Get @-mentions and /sf, read messages in its channels, DMs and group chats, and reply. Required.
web-pages.slackApp.group.canvases.descri: Create, edit and read canvases, e.g. plans and reports in a channel
web-pages.slackApp.group.channels.descri: Create channels, invite members, and see joins and new channels
web-pages.slackApp.group.connect.descrip: View, send and accept invites to channels shared with other companies
web-pages.slackApp.group.customize.descr: Set a display name and avatar per message
web-pages.slackApp.group.dm.description: Open DMs with one or more people
web-pages.slackApp.group.extras.descript: Unfurl links, set reminders, read DND and call status
web-pages.slackApp.group.files.descripti: Read attachments, upload screenshots, logs and other files
web-pages.slackApp.group.lists.descripti: Create, edit and read Slack Lists, e.g. task lists
web-pages.slackApp.group.more.descriptio: Set its presence, read message metadata and workspace settings, embed video links
web-pages.slackApp.group.connect.admin: Accepting invites needs the app installed by someone who can approve Slack Connect channels (admins, by default); sending them depends on workspace settings, and paid plans only
web-pages.slackApp.group.usergroups.admi: Creating and editing user groups requires workspace settings to allow it, and many workspaces limit it to admins; user groups are on paid plans only
web-pages.slackApp.group.people.descript: Read emails, profiles, user groups, workspace info and custom emoji
web-pages.slackApp.group.public.descript: Reply in public channels without an invite
web-pages.slackApp.group.reactions.descr: Mark progress with emoji, pin messages, manage bookmarks
web-pages.slackApp.group.search.descript: Search public messages and files and find people by name, to gather context
